description:
A feed, read aloud. Every minute it reads the feed it was given, and anything it has not spoken before is sent to a voice and the audio kept in the library.

The feed is the only thing it knows about its source, which is what makes it general: a reading list, a blog, a newsroom — anything that publishes RSS or Atom becomes a podcast without this board learning where it came from.

Two things are worth reading in the pipeline. The **claim** is one SQL statement doing the work of a lease: it takes the item, hands back nothing at all when the item is already spoken or is being spoken right now — and returning nothing stops that pass, which is how work is skipped — and gives back the path the episode is to be kept at, built from its identity rather than from a counter that would drift. An item claimed but never finished is offered again once its claim goes stale, so a voice that was down for an hour costs a delay rather than a silence nobody notices. And the **path comes back with the audio**, in a header the voice sets, because an answer arriving later than the pass that asked for it has to say what it is an answer to.

A round asks the feed for its ten newest and lets the claim decide which of those are work; nothing limits the iteration itself, because an Iterator cuts the list before the claim sees it and an article below the cut would never get another turn. The calls of one round are in flight together and a voice renders them in order, so the first full round on an empty library takes as long as everything in it put together.

Needs hkp-node on 8080 and a voice to call. Alone it points at the public Hacker News feed; in the composition the reading list is the feed instead.

What it has read aloud is published as a feed of its own, by the second runtime here. It has a clock rather than a trigger, for a structural reason worth knowing: an endpoint serving the last value it was handed answers with whatever its chain returns, so it has to be the last service in one — and the rendering chain above stops on the rounds where there is nothing new. A minute's staleness buys a feed that is rebuilt whatever happened.

The enclosure URLs point into the library, named rather than written down: the address is assigned when the board loads, and a Map is handed it the same way a client dialling it would be.

state.schema:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS episode (
  slug     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  guid     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  title    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  summary  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  link     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  feed     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  published TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  claimed  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  rendered TEXT,
  bytes    INTEGER
);
state.statement:
INSERT INTO episode (slug, guid, title, summary, link, feed, published)
VALUES (substr($slug, 1, 100), $id, $title, $summary, $link, $feed, $published)
ON CONFLICT(slug) DO UPDATE SET claimed = datetime('now')
  WHERE episode.rendered IS NULL
    AND episode.claimed < datetime('now', $retryAfter)
RETURNING 'episodes/' || slug || '.mp3' AS path, title, summary

UPDATE episode
   SET rendered = datetime('now'), bytes = $size
 WHERE 'episodes/' || slug || '.mp3' = $path

SELECT '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>'
    || '<rss version="2.0"><channel>'
    || '<title><![CDATA[' || replace(IFNULL($channelTitle, ''), ']]>', ']]>') || ']]></title>'
    || '<link>' || replace(replace(replace(IFNULL($channelLink, ''), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>') || '</link>'
    || '<description><![CDATA[' || replace(IFNULL($channelDescription, ''), ']]>', ']]>') || ']]></description>'
    || IFNULL(group_concat(item, '' ORDER BY sortKey DESC), '')
    || '</channel></rss>' AS feed
  FROM (
    SELECT '<item>'
        || '<title><![CDATA[' || replace(IFNULL(title, ''), ']]>', ']]>') || ']]></title>'
        || '<link>' || replace(replace(replace(IFNULL(link, ''), '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>') || '</link>'
        || '<guid isPermaLink="false">' || replace(replace(replace(slug, '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>') || '</guid>'
        || '<pubDate>' || IFNULL(published, '') || '</pubDate>'
        || '<description><![CDATA[' || replace(IFNULL(summary, ''), ']]>', ']]>') || ']]></description>'
        || '<enclosure url="' || replace(replace(replace(IFNULL($audioBase, '') || '/' || slug || '.mp3', '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>')
        || '" type="audio/mpeg" length="' || IFNULL(bytes, 0) || '"/>'
        || '</item>' AS item,
           rendered AS sortKey
      FROM episode
     WHERE rendered IS NOT NULL
     ORDER BY rendered DESC
     LIMIT 100
  )

SELECT title,
       IFNULL($base, '') || '/' || slug || '.mp3' AS url,
       IFNULL(published, '') AS published
  FROM episode
 WHERE rendered IS NOT NULL
 ORDER BY rendered DESC
 LIMIT 100

SELECT '#EXTM3U' || char(10)
    || IFNULL(group_concat(entry, char(10) ORDER BY sortKey), '')
    || char(10) AS playlist
  FROM (
    SELECT '#EXTINF:-1,' || replace(replace(IFNULL(json_extract(value, '$.title'), ''), char(13), ' '), char(10), ' ') || char(10)
        || IFNULL(json_extract(value, '$.url'), '') AS entry,
           key AS sortKey
      FROM json_each($rows)
  )

items.placeholder: Nothing is spoken twice: an article already in the ledger stops its own pass. The audio is written into the library volume, which the Library unit serves.
Everything the radio has read, newest first. Press play once and it runs on by itself; a track finishing starts the next one, and an episode rendered while you listen joins the end.
